title: Introduce traffic-rate-derivative sentinel and temporal dampening guard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a derivative-based throughput sentinel and temporal dampening guard to reduce false positives during rapid traffic ramp events. The feature is behind a config flag and off by default.
description: Motivation: existing canary detectors trigger on absolute throughput deltas and can produce false positives during short-lived traffic bursts or controlled ramps. This PR implements a derivative-based sentinel that evaluates the first derivative (rate-of-change) of throughput and couples it with a temporal dampening guard that suppresses automated rollbacks when derivative spikes are accompanied by low statistical confidence. Summary: new detector implementation, controller for adaptive cooldown, configuration knobs, unit and integration tests, and documentation. Key behavioral goals: 1) detect true regressions where throughput degrades gradually or abruptly without coincident high-frequency traffic noise; 2) avoid reactive rollbacks during short-lived ramp windows; 3) emit metrics and audit events for observability. Commits: 1) add derivative sentinel implementation and unit tests; 2) add temporal dampening controller, adaptive cooldown logic, and feature flag; 3) wire metrics and audit events, add integration harness test and dashboard links; 4) tuning and test fixes after review. Changed areas: perf-canary/pkg/detectors/derivative.go implements the detector and smoothing primitives; perf-canary/pkg/dampening/controller.go implements the temporal cooldown state machine and confidence scoring; perf-canary/config/canary_rules.yaml adds new rule schema entries for derivative_threshold, smoothing_window, and dampening_params; perf-canary/test/integration/derivative_integration_test.go adds synthetic ramp/inject scenarios; perf-canary/charts/perf-canary-values.yaml exposes the feature flag and default params; docs/perf-canary/derivative-sentinel.md describes config and operational guidance. Behaviour & signals: emits metric perfcanary.derivative.rate, perfcanary.dampening.active (boolean), and audit events perfcanary.dampening_applied with context. Deployment plan: feature is behind a runtime flag set to off by default; rollout to staging for 48h with synthetic ramp traffic, monitor dashboards and error budgets, then canary to a small subset of production traffic slices under supervision. Rollback plan: disable rule via config and redeploy; code remains dormant behind the flag so immediate removal is low-risk. Performance results: in staged synthetic experiments this approach reduced noisy automated rollbacks by ~62% while preserving recall above 93% for injected throughput regressions across three traffic shapes. Security/permissions: no elevation of privileges required. Compatibility: works with existing canary pipeline; graceful no-op if derivative metrics are not present. Follow-ups: ENG-2234 for auto-calibration of thresholds and ENG-2299 for multi-cohort dampening heuristics. Checklist: unit tests, integration tests, perf harness runs, docs updated.
review_conversation: Diego Martinez: Suggest smoothing derivative with EWMA and expose smoothing_window as a config knob; asked for clearer variable names in controller.go.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented EWMA smoothing, renamed variables as suggested, and added comments explaining confidence scoring math.
Fiona Liu: Requested an extra integration case with a stochastic ramp; author added deterministic seed and test harness update.
Omar Khalid: Verified emitted metrics and recommended adding an audit event when dampening suppresses a rollback; added event and small docs note.
Approvals: Diego Martinez approved after re-run; Fiona Liu approved; Omar Khalid approved.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature-flagged, defaults tuned to low sensitivity, and requires explicit enablement in production charts. Operators should watch perfcanary.dampening.active and perfcanary.derivative.rate during first 48h post-enable. Follow-up work planned for threshold auto-calibration (ENG-2234).
